messages.content: Write the note with these sections, in this order, and don't skip one: Decision, Risk, Rollback, Owner. The situation is a payments column old readers might not tolerate.

<think>
[frame: pathway=s2|mode=plan|construct=deeptree|persona=neutral|identity=none|theme=none|channel=reasoning]
Four sections, that order. Decision is the flag, not a default-on write. Risk is select-star and NOT NULL with no default. Rollback is the flag off, column left nullable. Owner is whoever has the payments pager. If I drop Rollback the note looks finished and isn't.
</think>

## Decision
Ship the column behind a flag. Don't make the new write the default.

## Risk
Old readers that select star, and inserts that omit the column, break if it is NOT NULL with no default.

## Rollback
Turn the flag off. Leave the column nullable. Don't drop it the same day.

## Owner
Whoever has the payments pager this week signs the flag-on.
Sections in this order, none skipped: Goal, Constraint, Step, Check. Moving invoice mail off the monolith without losing a receipt.

<think>
[frame: pathway=s2|mode=plan|construct=deeptree|persona=neutral|identity=none|theme=none|channel=reasoning]
Goal is the move without a lost receipt. Constraint is one engineer and the same vendor. Step is dual-write, cut, delete. Check is a day of ids in both logs, then only in the new one. The check is the part people skip, so it has to be its own section.
</think>

## Goal
Move invoice email off the monolith without losing a receipt.

## Constraint
One engineer, no feature freeze, the mail vendor stays.

## Step
Dual-write the receipt id, cut the sender, then delete the old sender.

## Check
A day of ids in both logs before the cut, and only in the new log after.
